# Contextual review and severity

Run `kodi_review context` (or `kodi-toolkit review-context ADDON`) once for bounded numbered sources and the exact input schema. Inspect related callers, manifest and settings; check guards, consent, redaction, disabled code and version mismatch. A keyword or hidden UI field alone proves no leak, encryption requirement or Kodi policy violation.

Use `model_findings`, `coverage` (scope, complete, reviewed_files), and nonempty `limitations`. Each finding needs category, title, mechanism (reachable operation and preconditions), reason (consequence), severity, confidence, project-verified add-on-relative path, one-based line and literal quote. Related evidence can support, counter or contextualize. State incomplete coverage. Empty findings are correct when no issue is supported.

| Classification | Criteria |
|---|---|
| Confirmed deterministic error | Actual failing syntax/types/manifest/package/checker stage; preserve its original diagnostic. |
| Evidence-supported contextual issue / material | Independent narrow source check supports a canonical conditional observation. Model prose is retained separately; execution and sensitive content remain unverified. |
| Recommendation / advisory | Nonbreaking improvement; no claimed validation failure. |
| Unverified observation | Structurally accepted or rejected claim without independent semantic support; advisory only in the classified output. |
| Blocker | Demonstrated inability to install/start or serious boundary failure, with bounded reproduction steps, observed and expected outcomes. Source anchoring alone is insufficient. |

Static traces use source-supported, omit reproduction, and describe conditional consequences. Never fill observed outcomes without an actual test. Demonstrated claims require an actual reproduction, which the contract cannot independently certify. A setting-to-log flow may support conditional privacy risk if the value is sensitive, but proves neither a real secret nor execution. Do not describe `xbmc.log` as stdout. WARN/INFO recommendations belong to checker findings unless distinct source behavior establishes a separate issue. Offline URL checks are unverified coverage, not a confirmed broken source.

Prefer `kodi_review compose` or `kodi-toolkit review-compose ADDON DRAFT --branch VERIFIED_BRANCH --cache CACHE`. Supply the draft only, not the context envelope. Prefer the native structured `report` object; the legacy `report_json` string remains supported but needs nested escaping. Never supply both. Composition runs independent checks, derives canonical checker records and discards draft checker claims. No extra validate call is needed. Correct rejected anchors/classification once, then report remaining rejection. `static_passed` describes checks, `contract_passed` describes the report. `passed` covers both only; semantic_verification remains human-required. A rejected model draft never changes a warning-only checker into a deterministic error. A reproduction description is still an author's claim until independently checked.

Primary policy revisions: https://kodi.wiki/index.php?title=Add-on_rules&oldid=263662 and https://kodi.wiki/index.php?title=Submitting_Add-ons&oldid=253238 . General contextual review concepts were researched against https://github.com/xbmc/kodiai/tree/545b9afa96695f7c97bf0e2ab214295ba45dd196 ; no proprietary code or prompts were copied.

Schema 1.3: `accepted_findings` means structural acceptance only. Use composition's `finding_categories`, never a model's confidence label, as the factual view. The small validator supports only an adjacent direct setting read/log pattern; it does not perform general data-flow proof. Literal messages, redaction, rebinding, counterevidence and unsupported patterns do not become supported defects. Canonical observations replace model prose in the supported view; original claims remain diagnostic material. Known `requirement_basis` IDs (`dependency-minimum`, `log-level-integer`) identify documentation only; unknown rules and applicability remain unverified. Duplicate anchors/categories and exact official messages are recorded separately. Paraphrase equivalence is not certified. A model-written reproduction cannot establish blocker severity.

Evaluation produces `final-report.json` and `final-report.md` mechanically from recorded calls, initial/current file hashes and completion gates. Use those for factual status; preserve useful model explanations separately as unverified prose. Incomplete replies/drafts are never PASS. Standalone callers can save CLI JSON and run `report-build`; records must come from trusted tools, not model-authored summaries.

# Validation stages
Identify the intended release, then use its documented isolated interpreter for both `-m kodi_agent_toolkit.cli stub-lanes` and `-m kodi_agent_toolkit.cli validate PATH --branch VERIFIED_BRANCH --cache CACHE`. Record actual Python/platform, exact installed Kodistubs/mypy/checker and qualification/readiness limits. Branch selection does not switch environments; missing setup is incomplete validation. The exposed kodi_validate tool runs the same wrapper for the disposable fixture; it does not execute add-on code.
Inspect every stage and preserve raw diagnostics: syntax, manifest/packaging, mypy with version-matched Kodistubs, official addon-check process. A warning-only checker run can exit zero. A timeout, traceback, missing cache or schema failure is not a clean result. Do not silently change .tests-config.json or install dependencies.
Official checker 0.0.36 makes remote index and URL requests even with --skip-dependency-checks. Toolkit execution replays explicitly acquired local index snapshots, blocks network, and preserves unverified-URL warnings. Cache setup is explicit and separate; validation never downloads add-on dependencies. Record snapshot hashes/date and target branch. Offline coverage is not live repository submission approval.
Syntax parsing does not import Kodi modules. Type checking is useful for API signatures but not runtime semantics. Stub/target version mismatches must be reported. Declared dependencies are not resolved by downloading their packages. Packaging checks concern the resulting add-on payload, not unrelated development files in its source repository.
For contextual review use review.md. After a source repair rerun affected stages, keeping old failing output. Report exact checks, warnings, skipped stages and no-runtime-test limitation.

# Development role boundaries

Apply the user's task, project instructions and actual client/server permissions
before using any role. Discover the selected Kodi version, source, owned workspace
and generation; never carry a historical target UUID into another installation.
Keep reusable workflow details in these skills rather than copying them into
every agent prompt. Available tools supply no task authorization or server grant.

- **Developer:** inspect the actual add-on manifest, reproduce the issue, edit only
  the approved source and run the release-matched static lane. For authorized Lab
  work follow [current contracts](current-contract.md): reviewed edit/import,
  exact-generation validation, preflight, admitted deployment, eligible launch and
  observation. Local files need an explicitly registered, synchronized source
  mirror before Lab can import them.
- **Runtime tester:** test the existing owned workspace. Do not edit source,
  create/import workspaces or repair infrastructure. Establish expected behavior,
  validate/preflight the same generation and deploy only when separately
  authorized and necessary. Use the validated manifest entry; fixed video smoke
  is not a generic Program-script launcher. Report blocked setup to its owner.
- **Inspector:** answer the requested diagnostic using only authorized target
  status, UI, inventory, bounded logs or images. Complete pagination before
  counting. Healthy status is not clean logs. Null UI fields are unknown. No
  navigation, deployment, execution, lifecycle or source edits.
- **Reviewer/repository manager:** preserve an existing project's independent
  review, artifact and publication policy. These roles are not automatically
  installed by the portable presets. Fixture adapters cannot qualify another
  project's source or release. Publication remains a separately authorized task.

Use only the tools needed for the question. Retain private receipts and warnings;
summarize source/workspace/generation, runtime/profile identity, actual observed
behavior, unresolved operations and next test. Static PASS, native readiness,

claims. Reuse valid current evidence rather than reset, recopy or redeploy by
habit. Preserve the original request identity after an uncertain operation.

Inspection does not navigate. Lifecycle, navigation, settings, recovery and
promotion require separate explicit policy/task authority; default daily presets
do not add them. Never expand your own configuration or use direct RPC, shell,
another credential or a new workspace to bypass a refusal. Exclude production

Images require current screenshot authorization and actual image content reaching

retrieval](mcp.md#action-observations-and-correlated-screenshots) and the current
contract's screenshot permissions; do not replay navigation to recover an image.

# Current trusted managed Kodi agent workflow

Source checkpoint: Kodi Lab main `574eeee5b3dd444ab651cab3b73071714bd95ff6` (2026-11-14). Read the [server's tool and permissions matrix](https://github.com/kcook98765/kodi-lab/blob/main/docs/MCP-TOOLS-AND-PERMISSIONS.md), [unattended source installation](https://github.com/kcook98765/kodi-lab/blob/main/docs/MANAGED-ADDON-INSTALLATION.md), [agent project contracts](https://github.com/kcook98765/kodi-lab/blob/main/docs/AGENT-PROJECTS.md), and [Reset/Bridge recovery](https://github.com/kcook98765/kodi-lab/blob/main/docs/MANAGED-AGENT-RESET.md) for exact schemas and limits. This guide does not grant permissions. An installed server may differ: discover its authenticated tool schemas before runtime work.

## Select the environment

- **Trusted Managed Lab:** the administrator explicitly enables Full Development for the agent. This role covers approved, already installed disposable versions and agent-owned projects. It can admit autonomous Reset with independent Bridge preparation, subject to human priority, lifecycle, native identity, replay and resource guards. It does **not** install/acquire missing Kodi versions or grant external access.
- **Managed read-only/custom client:** require applicable client/Kodi policies, exact target grant, and specific permissions. `managed.versions`, `managed.lifecycle` and `managed.reset` are not synonyms. A read-only credential must not mutate.
- **External Production:** inspect scope and exact grant; screenshots and restricted navigation separately default Off on each Kodi. Select/Context are prohibited. No source deployment, lifecycle or agent-owned managed role.
- **External Development:** exact grant plus verified capability maxima; no assumption that managed launch or project authority transfers. Never widen the role to work around a missing tool.

## Preferred agent-owned source loop

1. `managed_status({})` to discover installed versions and exact profile/runtime identity. Select `matrix`, `nexus`, `omega` or `piers`; current Piers has qualified RC2, but existing profiles may remain pinned to RC1. Call `managed_start` with saved UUID/version only when authorized. Wait for `native_ready`, then independently check live Bridge readiness. Observe the one-running policy and human viewer/control holds.
2. `project_create` with saved request UUID and fresh add-on ID for a private inert Program/video-plugin starter; or `project_import` with a reviewed source ZIP, SHA-256 and provenance. Small inline intake allows at most 45 KiB compressed. For up to 4 MiB compressed (1,024 entries, 16 MiB expanded), stage reviewed chunks through `project_transfer` and then `project_import` using the retained transfer identity. This private ownership path needs no manual Web source registration/Current Kodi selection. Do not adopt another client's project.
3. `project_status` and `workspace_status` until owned workspace seed/capture is ready. `workspace_tree`/`workspace_read` verify actual generation/file hashes. For paginated reads use returned `next_line` until complete before full-file replacements. `workspace_edit` requires actual `expected_generation` and bounded payload. Keep returned generation; never increment locally.
4. `workspace_validate` (structural) then `workspace_deploy_preflight` with exact workspace/generation/target (no reservation). On a typed blocker, stop and follow only the supported recovery. Never treat static Toolkit validation as equivalent to Lab validation.
5. `workspace_deploy` on explicit managed target with a new saved request UUID, exact generation, and `deployment_mode: "direct"`. Retain tree/deployment receipts; `verified_existing` means current bytes verified, not fresh execution. If first-copy program/video enablement leaves the native Disabled add-ons question on screen, only an authorized same-profile `managed_stop` then `managed_start` using two separately saved UUIDs may clear it. Verify same profile and readiness again; do not automate bypassing consent.
6. `workspace_launch` with declared `extension_ordinal`, target, generation and another saved UUID. `development_launch` is a distinct declared-entry option. `workspace_execute` is a bounded fixed workflow, never arbitrary shell or Python. Inspect `inspect_ui_state`, `log_read`, and actual screenshot pixels if authorized. `remote_action` needs target control and defers to human input ownership. `addon_settings_set`/ `addon_settings_result` require explicit declared-setting authority (`development.settings.write`); a settings receipt does not itself relaunch or execute.
7. Iterate new validated generations; stop with `managed_stop` to retain Kodi state. `managed_release` releases eligible lifecycle ownership, not the Kodi process. For another version, stop current then start the next and independently deploy/verify its bytes.

## Autonomous clean Reset (only when the task authorizes destruction)

Read `managed_status` and save exact `profile_identity` for selected version. Pass `expected_profile`, version, saved UUID and optional `restart` (defaults false) to `managed_reset`. A stale binding refuses. Reset destroys Kodi writable profile/settings/add-ons but not owned project, workspace, Git, other versions or unrelated host state. It is never routine recovery. Replays use the **original parameters and UUID**, even after ambiguous responses. The returned `phase=complete` denotes replacement, not Bridge readiness. Inspect separate `bridge_preparation` checkpoint/receipt and live trust after Start. Resume using an expressly offered `resume_bridge_version` from original receipt only when original child is proven terminal and idle. Re-establish deployment evidence on replacement; older selected-session workflows may need administrator re-binding while stopped.

## Other supported but separate routes

Existing **registered source** workspaces use `development_source_list` and exact grants, `workspace_create`, `workspace_import_preview`/`workspace_import`, optional `workspace_source_scan`/`workspace_capture`, then validate/preflight/deploy. `managed_selection_preview`/`managed_select` do not grant access, start Kodi, or create a fresh source baseline.

`package_import`/`package_status` and `package_install`/`package_install_status` retain/deliver an original installable ZIP, **not** native ZIP GUI installation (Kodi Lab issue #305). Repository installation by ID cannot silently select a reviewed exact package and remains unresolved (issue #339). Use source deployment for agent-directed unattended work. `promotion_request` requests human review for eligible registered-source projects; never publishes and excludes agent-owned projects.

## Recovery and evidence

Hold the original UUID, exact arguments, profile, target, source/workspace/generation, current file hashes and operation receipt. A timeout, pending result or client output-schema error does not mean the server did nothing. Inspect receipt-first and never create a different request ID for unresolved work. Missing grants, human viewers, Bridge identity mismatch, reconciliation and capacity are not invitations to alter permissions, re-pair devices, call direct Kodi RPC, reset or bypass fences.

Report separately: source changed; static Toolkit validation; Lab structural validation; deployment preflight; deployed exact bytes; launch dispatched; native result observed; functional behavior verified. Limit claims to the tested Kodi release, exact profile/runtime, native host and workflow. Keep credentials, screenshots and logs private.

Do not require manually registered sources for this route. Registered-source workflows below remain valid for existing sources. Autonomous Reset needs task-level destructive authority, expected_profile and a separately verified Bridge preparation receipt. Original ZIP delivery and repository installation by ID are not equivalent to unattended source deployment.

contract's [managed lifecycle section](current-contract.md#opt-in-managed-version-lifecycle).

## Efficient development loop

Use the installed server's exposed schemas and existing grants. Discover the intended target/version with `target_list` and the source with `development_source_list`; use `workspace_status` to find or resume the matching owned workspace before creating another. Inspect only the tree/files needed for the task. Missing source registration, grants or target setup is an operator blocker; report it without inventing IDs, changing permissions or recreating infrastructure.

1. Record the workspace, source, target and current generation. Reuse current validation/deployment evidence and assess prerequisites. Expected source-baseline staleness after workspace deployment is distinct from missing provenance; follow [workspace provenance and failure decisions](current-contract.md#calls-and-evidence). If a source baseline is genuinely missing, follow the preflight's stated administrator preparation path only with applicable mutation authority; do not automatically deploy or repeat a verified baseline on resume.
2. Group related edits, carrying forward the generation returned by each edit. Validate the resulting generation with `workspace_validate`; static validation does not prove runtime behavior.
3. Read `workspace_deploy_preflight` for that workspace, exact generation and target. Its durable-prerequisite verdict is blocked or unknown, never ready; follow the stated actor/preconditions without treating it as admission. When separately authorized and eligible, deploy that exact validated generation with `workspace_deploy`. Confirm completed deployment and matching target/add-on evidence before executing. An accepted request, healthy target or unchanged add-on version alone is not deployment proof.
4. Launch the validated manifest entry with authorized `workspace_launch` and observe fresh-code execution and relevant behavior using bounded logs/UI evidence. Use `workspace_execute` when its fixed smoke operation fits the task. Record the observed outcome; deployment or dispatch alone is not functional acceptance.
5. Recheck only changed behavior or failed/stale evidence. On an ordinary generation conflict, refresh status and the affected file before editing again; revalidate the new generation before deployment.

The direct-workspace lane is **Inspect → Edit → Validate → Deploy → Launch/Observe
→ Repeat**, retaining the required preflight and mutation-time admission above.
Use `workspace_edit` in the existing authorized workspace without unnecessary
source recopy/preparation, whole-tree rereads or repeated status queries. Program
54's two successful changed-code iterations took about 41.43 and 41.50 seconds,
eight MCP calls each; observation varies by task, so this is neither a required
call count nor a reason for a combined tool. Keep original test content/hash;
restore through a new supported edit, validate/deploy/launch/observe that generation,
and accept generation advancement rather than reset history (Program 54: 37→40).

For an in-progress operation, retain its request/operation ID and inspect status using the installed server's documented completion mechanism. A timeout or ambiguous result does not prove failure. Preserve the receipt and uncertainty; do not dispatch another mutation, create a replacement workspace or invent a new request ID to force progress. Report any reconciliation or administrator action required. Stop once the requested result is verified.

## Registered-source batch import

When reviewed changes are already in the registered source mirror, prefer
`workspace_import_preview(workspace_id, expected_generation)` over individual
file edits. Lab does not read arbitrary paths on the agent's computer. Import
requires workspace edit and source inspection permissions, the exact source
grant and the client's workspace binding; an available tool grants none of these.

Review the preview's paths, sizes, hashes and rejections. Pass its `source_digest`
and `preview_digest` to `workspace_import` with the same workspace/generation and
a fresh UUID `request_id`. The accepted batch creates one generation; validate
and deploy that exact returned generation separately. Import does not run Kodi.
A changed source or workspace requires a fresh preview.

At the audited source revision the limits are 32 changed entries and 256 KiB per UTF-8 file; use the preview's advertised bounds. Parents must already exist.
Default `changes` mode rejects deletions, binary files, identity/mode changes and overlapping private edits without partial application. A later import can update a previously
imported file while its workspace bytes still match the prior import receipt.
Use `workspace_edit` for eligible focused private changes; preserve existing
private edits and import history instead of resetting them to force an import.

When exposed and explicitly intended, `mode="reviewed_tree"` in both preview and apply supports reviewed workspace file removals and exact per-path conflict choices (`take_source` or `keep_private`). Review the resolved preview and repeat its mode, resolutions, source and preview digests exactly in apply. No wildcard force exists; directory/type/mode/identity changes remain unsupported. `matches_source=true` describes the staged private tree, while retained private choices describe a reviewed merge. These removals do not authorize deletion of installed Kodi destination files. See the maintained [batch-import contract](https://github.com/kcook98765/kodi-lab/blob/main/docs/WORKSPACE-BATCH-IMPORT.md).

After a lost import response, repeat only the identical request UUID and
parameters to recover its receipt through the documented idempotent recovery.
That recovery does not capture newer source bytes or dispatch the import again.
Retain `reconciliation_required` outcomes for administrator review; do not replay
an uncertain import with a new request ID.

## Launching and relaunching an add-on

Before launch, verify the matching installation is enabled and no unresolved
modal blocks the task. Inspect the exact native dialog and its effects; never
blindly dismiss confirmations. In the investigated Kodi 21.3 **Disabled add-ons**
startup dialog, **No** left the add-on disabled, recorded the USER-disabled reason
and suppressed future prompts. Copy/deploy does not enable a disabled add-on.
Respect agent interaction restrictions: where needed, hand off guarded enablement
of the exact intended add-on to an authorized administrator, preserving runtime,
source/dependency, CSRF and separate service-start consent guards. Verify its
receipt and enabled inventory before resuming. This grants no arbitrary dialog
selection or new MCP enable capability.

Identify the manifest-declared script/plugin entry point and intended destination before navigating. A package with both extensions can open its plugin directory from a generic Run action even when the test needs its custom script window. Verify the actual destination rather than treating any successful invocation as GUI acceptance.

For an already deployed add-on on a managed development profile, prefer
`workspace_launch` when exposed and authorized. Use a fresh `request_id`,
`workspace_id`, exact `expected_generation`, `target_id` and the chosen
`extension_ordinal` from validation's `launch_entries`. Ordinals follow manifest
order starting at zero; discover them instead of assuming the script/plugin order.
Reuse valid validation/deployment evidence for unchanged bytes. A legacy validation
may need one refresh to publish launch entries.

Launch requires target control and development execution authority, current
workspace/source bindings, usable Kodi, enabled matching installed bytes and a
compatible trusted managed Bridge. It cannot launch external/production targets
or start Kodi. Updating Lab alone does not upgrade an installed Bridge. An
`accepted` receipt proves dispatch only; inspect the intended destination and
feature behavior. Recover an uncertain launch using its identical request and
documented receipt mechanism; do not issue a new launch or menu invocation while
dispatch remains ambiguous.

If deployment is independently verified and a direct launch is definitively
rejected before dispatch, such as `launch_not_deployed`, retain the rejection and
use an already authorized, verified menu route when available. Do not repeatedly
redeploy unchanged bytes, reset the workspace or alter the manifest to force the
launcher. Missing authority or unverified deployment remains a blocker.

`workspace_execute` is a bounded smoke workflow, not a generic launcher: check its documented eligibility before using it for a script or multi-extension package. Record an unsupported entry point once and use the supported fallback; do not repeat the incompatible operation after each edit or change the manifest merely to satisfy it.

When menu navigation is required, find the shortest working route once and retain its labels, starting state and expected destination with the test evidence. Reuse an add-on-provided launch item, or a verified favourite if creating one is within the task's authority. Confirm that the shortcut opens the intended entry point. Before replaying a route, check current UI state; adapt if a dialog, skin or menu changed. Reuse deployment evidence and the route across iterations without rediscovering the whole add-on inventory.

Use structured UI state for navigation decisions and screenshots for visual questions. Keep remote actions ordered; use a bounded action sequence only if the exposed interface explicitly supports it, otherwise call actions sequentially. Observe at state transitions and before a consequential selection; do not add a screenshot/model round trip after every arrow by habit. Neither successful dispatch nor a plugin listing proves the expected custom window loaded. Keep launch latency separate from add-on callback/render measurements.

## Action observations and correlated screenshots

On managed development targets, request `remote_action(observe_ui=true)` when the
installed schema supports it and the client has inspection authority as well as
control. Reuse a fresh, sufficient `post_action_observation` for the next decision
instead of immediately requesting the same UI state again. Observation status,
time and `changed_during_collection` still determine whether the result is usable;
observation failure does not change the action's outcome.

When pixels are needed, use `screenshot_retrieve` on the original client connection
with that action's exact `target_id`, original `request_id` and `capture_id`.
Current screenshot authority and the same runtime identity are required. At the
2026-11-09 checkpoint capture/retrieve use `target.inspect`; do not infer a
mandatory extra `target.visual` grant from historical wording. Retrieval
returns the correlated frame without a new capture or navigation. Images expire
after two minutes and can be replaced sooner; an unavailable frame is not newer
visual evidence and does not justify repeating the action. Recover the original
receipt through its documented mechanism or request a fresh authorized observation
when needed. These capture-reuse tools initially cover managed development only.

Capture metadata alone is not an image. For a capture-in-progress result, follow
documented status/retry semantics without resending navigation to recover pixels.
Generic custom-window state or null labels may still require a visual check.

Keep full receipts, logs and inventories in the appropriate private/project evidence store. Carry a concise checkpoint containing the current/deployed generations, operation IDs, unresolved outcomes, next test and verified launch route across long sessions. Limit routine tool output to results, retained warnings and artifact references; read full details for the failure or visual question being investigated. Preserve required checks and exact-generation provenance.

# Dependency interpretation

See [official addon.xml dependency semantics](https://kodi.wiki/view/Addon.xml#version_attribute).
